name: ESP-01 / ESP-01S (ESP8266)
summary: The cheapest way to put WiFi on something, and the most awkward. Two usable GPIO, both strapping pins, and no on-board regulator. Orientation below has the antenna on the right.
notes: CH_PD must be pulled HIGH for the chip to run at all. On the original ESP-01, CH_PD left floating does nothing, and this is the single most common reason one appears dead. The ESP-01S has pull-ups on CH_PD and RST already.

Only GPIO0 and GPIO2 are brought out as general I/O, and both are strapping pins. GPIO0 low at boot enters flash mode; GPIO2 must be high at boot. That leaves very little room for a pull-down on either.

No on-board regulator and no 5 V tolerance anywhere. Feed it a clean 3.3 V that can deliver 300 mA peaks. The 3.3 V pin on a USB-serial adapter usually cannot, and the symptom is random resets during WiFi association.
TX and RX are 3.3 V. The module's RX is not 5 V tolerant, so a 5 V Arduino needs a divider on that line.
No ADC pin is brought out, and neither is GPIO15 or GPIO16, so deep-sleep wake is not possible without soldering to the chip.
The ESP-01S has 1 MB flash and moves the on-board LED to GPIO2. The original blue ESP-01 has 512 KB and its LED on the TX pin.
The 2x4 header is on 2.54 mm pitch but the two rows are only 0.1 inch apart, so it does not straddle a breadboard center channel. Use an adapter or jumpers.
Needs checking: which pins sit on the outer and inner rows hasn't been confirmed against an official Ai-Thinker drawing.

pins.name: TX
pins.note: Also the boot log output. High at boot; pulling it low stops the chip starting.

pins.name: CH_PD
pins.note: Must be tied high, through 10k to 3.3 V. Nothing runs until it is. The ESP-01S has this pull-up on board.

pins.name: RST
pins.note: Pull low to reset. Leave floating or pull high in normal use.

pins.name: 3V3
pins.note: Supply input, not an output. Needs 300 mA of headroom for transmit bursts.

pins.name: GPIO2
pins.note: Strapping pin: must be high at boot. Has an internal pull-up. One of only two usable I/O.

pins.name: GPIO0
pins.note: Strapping pin: low at boot enters flash mode. A button to ground here is fine, a steady load is not.

pins.name: RX
pins.note: Not 5 V tolerant. A 5 V Arduino TX needs a divider into this pin.
